fix(docs): one code font for code and output; narrow widths drawn by Panel alone; cards stay inside tips on phones (rich-docs-examples-xuu.8fh)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(docs): the example widget — code, and the output it produces, as one card (rich-docs-examples-xuu.8fh)

Every example on a migrated page is one element: VitePress's own highlighted
fence, and under it an output panel whose label strip names where the output
came from ("Output — produced by running the code above"), then the light and
dark fragments, CSS picking one per colour mode, or the marker's note. Labels
and captions are rows of the marker table beside the notes.

The fragment's font is the one thing a host can now set through its
all:initial, as the --rich-fragment-font custom property; the widget sets it to
the code font at a line height where box drawing joins. The blink keyframes are
included once through VitePress's head, from HTML_FRAGMENT_CSS. The light code
theme is one-light, so code and output share the One palette in both modes.

panel.md is migrated: its hand-drawn outputs are gone, and the narrow-widths
diagram is now an example that draws it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(docs): run every migrated page's examples at build time (rich-docs-examples-xuu.812) (#172)

* feat(docs): run every migrated page's examples at build time (rich-docs-examples-xuu.812)

A pre-transform Vite plugin builds each page's examples into one program
(imports hoisted, the barrel-and-console prelude, the page's exampleContext,
blocks chained in nested scopes), type-checks it under the repo's strict
options, bundles it, and runs it once under the simulated process in a 75x24
truecolor terminal. Each block's bytes are held to its marker, decoded with
decodeAnsi and encoded as a light and a dark fragment under its fence.
Every failure fails the build at the page and line.

The marker vocabulary and the fence parser are one module, which
test/docs/code-blocks.ts now reads too, so a marked block stays in the
symbol-existence sweep. Every page with a TypeScript fence starts on
NOT_YET_MIGRATED, so the site is unchanged. tscTransform moved out of
vitest.config.ts so the bundler compiles src/ the same way.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(docs): examples blame the context that threw; silent shows its note alone; ts{2} is TypeScript (rich-docs-examples-xuu.812)

Review of #172:
- a context throw is reported at the exampleContext, not the first block;
  splitRecords says whether the context finished
- the context is the chain's first scope, so it may redeclare console
- a silent block's note stands in place of output, with no empty fragments
- VitePress fence attributes ({2}, :line-numbers, [title]) no longer hide a
  TypeScript fence from every reader
- a default-plus-named import binds both names, so the prelude does not
  import the named one again
- a page runs once per docs:build, not once per VitePress build pass
- ExampleCompiler keeps parsed files by mtime, as its header claimed

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(docs): output ends its HTML block; the run cache follows src/; a non-Error throw has no orphan colon (rich-docs-examples-xuu.812)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(docs): one bundler for every simulated run; a thrown value shows as Node reports it (rich-docs-examples-xuu.812)

Review of #172 (CI reviewer):
- test/docs/bundle-program.ts is gone; its unit and e2e callers bundle with
  bundleExample, so the keepProcessEnv workaround has one home
- an exampleContext whose code is not indented fails instead of running empty
- barrel exports are read through resolveAlias
- `import type { X }` from the main barrel no longer stops the prelude
  importing X's value
- a throws block shows Error.prototype.toString, or `Uncaught <value>`, so an
  empty throw still shows
- a hyperlink passes the escape check (test)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(docs): a CRLF page is read like any other; one fewer helper (rich-docs-examples-xuu.812)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(docs): a barrel type import meets the name-collision check (rich-docs-examples-xuu.812)

A type-only import of a barrel value was filtered out before the check
that two imports may not bind one name differently, so another block
binding that name elsewhere silently won. It is now hoisted as the value
import it stands for, which dedupes against the same import and collides
with any other.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(docs): a program that does not bundle names its page (rich-docs-examples-xuu.812)

Every other failure the runner reports is prefixed with the page; a
bundler rejection (an import that type-checks but ships no JavaScript)
propagated bare.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(docs): the fence scanner reads every CommonMark fence form (rich-docs-examples-xuu.812)

An indented or tilde fence was invisible to both the runner and the
symbol-existence sweep, and prose starting with ```ts``` opened a fence
that mispaired every one after it. The sweep now calls scanFences
directly; extractCodeBlocks and CodeBlock were aliases of it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(docs): examples merge imports by export, assume barrel types, and stop on a stalled run (rich-docs-examples-xuu.812)

- An import is now a binding of a local name to an export, so a type and a
  value import of one export merge from any entry point, not only the main
  barrel; the barrelType special case is gone.
- The prelude imports the main barrel's types as well as its values, which
  is what docs/introduction.md tells readers.
- A run that has not finished after 5 s fails at the block it waits in.
- The prelude writes its own sentinel, so a throw there is no longer blamed
  on the page's exampleContext.
- The plugin takes its source stamp as an argument; its test no longer
  rewrites src/index.ts's mtime.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(docs): a character split across writes decodes whole; the runner header stops enumerating its checks (rich-docs-examples-xuu.812)

Byte writes were decoded one chunk at a time, so a multi-byte character
split across two writes became U+FFFD. The header's list of failures had
drifted from the checks twice; it now states the one claim, and the
deadline says it catches a run that waits, not one that spins.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
